summary.title: From Chatbot to Digital Colleague: The Paradigm Shift Toward Persistent Autonomous AI

details: LLM research is fragmenting across reasoning models, tool-calling agents, and workstation-style assistants, with no unified account of how these lines connect; the guiding question shifts from 'how to generate a better answer?' to 'how can an AI system reliably turn user intent into completed work?'

A survey organizing the evolution of LLM systems along two coupled dimensions: the cognitive core (Chatbot fast response -> Thinking LLM deliberate reasoning) and tool-augmented task execution (Agent environment-action-feedback loop -> OpenClaw-style persistent workstation).

Central claim: the 'Workspace + Skill' pairing (durable files/terminals/logs/permissions plus reusable, file-system-level skill packages with checks and constraints) is the mechanism that converts episodic chat and ad-hoc tool calls into persistent, verifiable 'digital colleague' work.

Corollary claim: this shift reframes data (instruction-response pairs -> CoT/process rewards -> state-action-observation trajectories) and evaluation (static answer accuracy -> sandboxed task closure, reliability, auditability, governance).
Part I: cognitive core, from scaling/parametric knowledge compression, alignment (RLHF, Constitutional AI, DPO) and multimodal expansion to long CoT, inference-time scaling, and RL-driven reasoning.

Part II: tool-augmented execution, from ReAct-style agent loops and the four capabilities (perception, planning, memory, tool use) to workspace intelligence, skill-based task closure, reliability and governance.
Part III: argument for Workspace + Skill, including an OpenClaw case study and an explicit limitations analysis.
Part IV: data and evaluation paradigm shifts across the three eras; plus open challenges and socio-technical roadmap.

Cognitive core: GPT-1/2/3/4, Chinchilla/Gopher scaling, MoE lines (Mixtral, DeepSeek-V2/V3), o1, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3 hybrid thinking, GPT-5 routing; RL algorithms PPO, GRPO, DAPO, Dr. GRPO, CISPO, GSPO, SAPO.

Agents: ReAct, Reflexion, Self-Refine, ToT/GoT, Toolformer, Gorilla, ToolLLM/ToolBench, MCP, GUI agents (Set-of-Mark, CogAgent, UI-TARS), memory systems (MemGPT, Generative Agents, Mem0, MEM1, Memory-R1).
Workstation systems: OpenClaw, OpenHands, SWE-agent, Anthropic Agent Skills (SKILL.md packages), Voyager skill libraries, harness engineering (SemaClaw, Sema Code).
Safety/governance: OpenClaw PRISM, ClawGuard, ClawKeeper, OS-Harm, agentic forensics, skill supply-chain analyses.
Chatbot era: pretraining corpora plus instruction/preference data (FLAN, Super-NaturalInstructions, Self-Instruct/Alpaca, LIMA, HH-RLHF, UltraFeedback).
Thinking era: long-CoT traces, self-training (STaR), math distillation (MetaMath, WizardMath, MAmmoTH, ToRA), process supervision (PRM800K, Math-Shepherd), verifiable-reward RL.

Agent/OpenClaw era: state-action-observation trajectories with tool calls, DOM/screenshots, terminal output, file diffs, permission boundaries, and reusable skill directories as first-class data assets.
Static benchmarks: MMLU/MMLU-Pro, MMMU, GSM8K, MATH, GPQA, LiveCodeBench, FrontierMath, HLE, IFEval, MT-Bench/Arena; process-level ProcessBench, PRMBench.
Agentic/environmental benchmarks: AgentBench, WebArena, WorkArena, OSWorld, SWE-bench, GAIA, Terminal-Bench, tau-bench, TheAgentCompany, ClawsBench, ClawBench, ATBench-Claw.

Proposed benchmark requirements: reproducible initial states, executable workspaces, full trajectory logs, final-state verification, cost/efficiency records, repeated-run consistency, and safety checks beyond single-run success rate.

key_findings.finding: The paper's organizing contribution is a two-dimensional taxonomy (cognitive core x tool-augmented execution) with four eras, plus an explicit definitional boundary separating Agent-era systems from OpenClaw-era workstation systems.
key_findings.evidence: A boundary table contrasts the two eras along organizing abstraction, unit of action, state model, knowledge reuse, task objective, evaluation focus, failure recovery, and safety boundary: the Agent era's minimal architecture is an environment-action-feedback loop, whereas the OpenClaw era requires the environment to act as a persistent host with durable files, sessions, logs, skills, and permissions.

key_findings.finding: Workspace + Skill is identified as the decisive mechanism turning episodic interaction into durable digital-colleague work: workspaces supply state, evidence and recoverability while skills supply reusable procedural memory.
key_findings.evidence: Argued via convergent evidence from OpenHands and SWE-agent (agent-computer interface as a design object), Voyager's executable skill library, and Anthropic/OpenClaw SKILL.md directory-level skill packages, together with an OpenClaw case study formalizing a four-stage loop of intent-to-workspace mapping, skill activation, workspace execution, and final-state verification.

key_findings.finding: Four structural bottlenecks of the Agent era are synthesized as architectural rather than prompting/scaling problems.
key_findings.evidence: Fragmented perception, ephemeral tool invocation, brittleness under environmental uncertainty, and absence of long-horizon task closure, derived from benchmark evidence (e.g., GPT-4 reaching only ~14% success on WebArena, success rates decaying super-linearly with horizon length) and failure taxonomies including hallucinated actions that cause irreversible errors.

key_findings.finding: The learning unit and evaluation target shift jointly: from instruction-response pairs to state-action-observation trajectories, and from answer accuracy to task closure with reliability and auditability.
key_findings.evidence: A data-paradigm table and staged review trace supervision from static corpora to long-CoT and step-level process rewards (PRM800K, Math-Shepherd) to environment logs with DOM/screenshots/terminal output; evaluation correspondingly moves to execution-verified environments (OSWorld, SWE-bench, ClawsBench) and to decomposed reliability metrics (consistency, robustness, recoverability, bounded error severity) rather than one-off success rates.

key_findings.finding: The paper argues persistence and reuse are not free: Workspace + Skill introduces new failure modes requiring lifecycle governance.
key_findings.evidence: A limitations analysis enumerates skill brittleness under environmental drift (UI redesigns, dependency/schema changes), procedural overfitting and negative transfer from automatic skill retrieval, workspace contamination by stale or partial artifacts, skill supply-chain attacks, and rising governance/evaluation cost; cited security work reports that agentized runtimes are riskier than the underlying models alone, motivating runtime enforcement layers such as PRISM and ClawGuard.
